findings.title: updateMany with empty data does not bump updatedAt
findings.body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is called with an empty data object. Prisma's `updateMany` with no fields to set does not reliably issue an update, so `@updatedAt` is not refreshed. The stated goal of touching `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is therefore not met, and the call costs an extra query on every cache refresh.

findings.title: Cache deletion doesn't invalidate connectedCalendars query
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation's `onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. It never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. As a result the dropdown keeps showing the old "Last updated" cache status until a manual refetch, which this page disables on window focus. The disconnect mutation does invalidate this query; deleteCache should do the same.

findings.title: Timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
findings.body: The cache timestamp is formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` instead of the user's locale. The surrounding text is translated, but non-English users will still see a US-format date.

findings.title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError
findings.body: A missing or unauthorized credential throws a plain `Error`. tRPC reports this as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN, so a client-side access error is surfaced as a server failure.

findings.title: sed -i '' is macOS-only
findings.body: `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed (Linux), the empty string is treated as the script and the command fails, so the env file is never updated. The relative path `ENV_FILE` also means the script only works when run from a specific directory.

findings.title: Cache status shown even when calendar-cache feature disabled
findings.body: The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly and queries the DB, bypassing the feature-flag mock used elsewhere. Stale cache rows can therefore be shown, and can be deleted from the UI, even when calendar-cache is disabled for the user.
